title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics, schema mapping, and tool message formatting
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: Align Redwood's OpenAI-compat layer with the latest function/tool-calling semantics used by mainstream models. This PR implements robust handling for model-emitted tool_choice objects, a best-effort mapping from OpenAI-style JSON Schema 'parameters' to Redwood's tool schema registry, and consistent message formatting for tool invocation and tool responses so downstream SDKs and the runtime can interpret tool calls consistently. Summary of changes: 1) Add a tool_choice response path in the compat response mapper that extracts name/arguments, validates arguments against a mapped schema, and emits a normalized ToolInvocation event to the runtime. 2) Implement schema mapping utilities that translate OpenAI 'parameters' into our compact tool schema (type coercion, required/optional mapping, property flattening heuristics for common patterns). 3) Update message formatting rules such that tool calls are represented as assistant messages with metadata (tool:name, tool_args_schema_version) for non-OpenAI consumers, while still supporting legacy function messages and direct tool responses. 4) Streaming: preserve streaming chunks for tool_choice but inject a lightweight tool-invocation boundary event so streaming clients (SDKs) can surface partial outputs and final tool args. 5) SDK changes: Python and TypeScript SDKs expose ToolInvocation and add helpers to register schema mappings and to pretty-print tool messages for logs. 6) Tests and docs: unit tests for mapper/schema utilities, integration tests against the openai-compat fixture models, and a new docs page describing migration and examples. Backwards compatibility: the compat layer accepts both legacy function messages and the new tool_choice path. For two release cycles we will warn on logs when patterns look like the legacy format; runtime routing prefers tool_choice when present. Migration notes: customers using custom tool registries should add a minimal schema mapping entry (examples in docs) to ensure argument coercion; if no mapping exists we fall back to JSON Schema validation against the declared parameters and surface an actionable error back to the caller. CI and release: test coverage added for corner cases (arrays of objects, nested optional fields, boolean coercion); performance test showed negligible impact when schema mapping cache is warm. See linked Linear tasks for rollout plan and docs updates.
commits: feat(openai-compat): add tool_choice handling and ToolInvocation event emitter
fix(openai-compat): fallback to function messages for legacy models
feat(sdk-python): expose ToolInvocation types and helpers
feat(sdk-ts): pretty-print tool messages and register-schema helper
test(openai-compat): add unit/integration tests for schema mapping
docs(openai-compat): add migration guide and examples
release_notes: Adds full support for model-emitted tool_choice semantics in the OpenAI-compat layer, including schema mapping utilities and SDK helpers. Backwards compatible with legacy function messages; migration docs provided.
